receipts.first_text_witness: Leo is sitting on the toilet at 7:14 in the morning in a pair of gym shorts he's owned since 2019, scrolling his brokerage app while his coffee gets cold on the bathroom counter. He's not expecting anything special. He checks the app every morning the same way some people check the weather. It's a habit.
receipts.last_text_witness: Leo put his phone down. He didn't text his wife. He didn't post about it. He made himself a piece of toast, finished his coffee, and went to a 9:00 a.m. meeting because he had a deadline that afternoon. That's what hitting 1 million looks like in real life. A piece of toast and a deadline and honestly that's a much better version than the one they sold you on. Drop a like if this gave you a different way to think about the milestone. I'll see you in the next one.

primary_source_receipts.finding: May CPI-U values 29.5, 129.2 and 335.123 imply $1 million in May 1960 equals about $11.36 million in May 2026 and $1 million in May 1990 equals about $2.594 million. The rounded claims are supported; purchasing power fell about 91.2% relative to 1960.

UBS supports more than 379,000 new U.S. USD millionaires in 2024 and 60 million, or 1.6% of sampled adults, globally. It measures net wealth per adult, not $1 million invested; the transcript silently changes both wealth definition and unit of analysis.

Ramsey reports eight in ten used a company 401(k), 94% lived below their means, 31% drove Toyota or Honda, only 5% reached millionaire net worth within ten years and a 25-30 year average. This self-reported study concerns net-worth millionaires and does not support the transcript's invented five-of-eighteen street split or a causal claim about any habit.
Morningstar supports 3.9% only for a modeled 30-year fixed-real-spending case, 30%-50% equity allocation and 90% success target. The transcript reports the number but omits important assumptions.
SSA estimated $2,071 per month for all retired workers after the 2026 COLA, not $2,081. The transcript is $10 per month high.

The four-person guideline is $33,000 in the contiguous United States and D.C., $41,250 in Alaska and $37,950 in Hawaii. Calling $39,000 the federal poverty line for a family of four is contradicted for the general U.S. claim and confuses guidelines with Census thresholds.

Traditional distributions are generally included in taxable income and qualified Roth distributions are generally tax-free, but tax depends on annual withdrawals, filing status, other income, basis and jurisdiction. Qualified-plan distributions are not net investment income for NIIT, though they can raise MAGI. A universal 25% haircut and $1.33 million equivalence are unsupported.

The weighted online survey supports that 36% of respondents with $1 million or more in investable assets considered themselves wealthy, hence 64% did not. It measures self-description, not objective financial adequacy.

Schwab supports a $2.3 million national average response for being wealthy. Exact 2025 San Francisco and Southern California values were not independently reproduced from the located national report and remain limited.
Empower reports a $5.3 million average net-worth response among 2,203 surveyed adults. It is a perception mean, not a median or prescriptive target.

The adversarial collaboration found continued association for the majority through the observed high-income range, with flattening among the least-happy subgroup. It does not prove that happiness rises forever, and income association is not proof of hedonic adaptation to portfolio milestones.

primary_source_receipts.claim: Compound returns and historical real-return context
primary_source_receipts.finding: SEC guidance describes long-run stock returns near 10% nominal and 6%-7% real, with substantial risk and long recovery periods. The rule-of-72 arithmetic at 8% is valid, but 8% real is an aggressive assumed constant return rather than a guaranteed S&P 500 outcome.

calculation_receipts.assumptions: Frozen views and age_days; exact listed same-channel long-form peers under build_baseline.compare; first five listed peers for sensitivity.

calculation_receipts.method: Independent inflation, income, tax and compounding arithmetic
calculation_receipts.assumptions: CPI uses same-month May CPI-U. Dividend arithmetic merely reproduces the transcript's unverified 1.06% yield. Federal tax illustrations assume the $39,000 traditional-plan withdrawal is the only 2026 income, no credits or itemization and no state tax. Compounding assumes a constant annual return with no fees, tax or volatility.
